abstract: In 2004, the spectral integral method (SIM) was proposed to solve TM$_z$ scattering by homogeneous two-dimensional dielectric objects and perfect electrical conductors with smooth boundaries. Its error decreases exponentially as the number of boundary points increases linearly. Plasmonic resonances, however, require TE$_z$ polarization and permittivities with a negative real part. The extension of SIM to this case shows that the original global singularity subtraction suffers catastrophic cancellation, with a round-off floor that grows exponentially with the attenuation accumulated across the object. To resolve this issue, this work introduces a windowed singularity subtraction that limits this cancellation amplification to an exponential factor that the user can set independently of the object size, provided the window is adequately resolved. Numerical results verify the accuracy of the proposed method.
